gloss: to accumulate; to store up; to build up

definitions.gloss: to accumulate; to store up; to build up
definitions.explanation: To gradually collect and store something over time, whether tangible (wealth, data) or intangible (experience, fatigue).

examples.japanese: {疲労|ひろう}が{蓄積|ちくせき}している。
{長年|ながねん}の{経験|けいけん}を{蓄積|ちくせき}してきた。
examples.english: I have accumulated years of experience.

examples.japanese: データを{蓄積|ちくせき}して{分析|ぶんせき}することで、{新|あたら}しい{知見|ちけん}が{得|え}られる。
examples.english: By accumulating and analyzing data, new insights can be obtained.

examples.japanese: ストレスを{蓄積|ちくせき}させないように、{定期的|ていきてき}に{休息|きゅうそく}を{取|と}ろう。
examples.english: Let's take regular breaks so stress doesn't build up.

notes:
Emphasizes gradual, layered accumulation over time. Used in both positive contexts (knowledge, experience, wealth) and negative ones (fatigue, stress, waste). More formal than {溜|た}まる.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {疲労|ひろう}の{蓄積|ちくせき}: accumulation of fatigue
- データの{蓄積|ちくせき}: accumulation of data
- {知識|ちしき}を{蓄積|ちくせき}する: to build up knowledge
- {資本|しほん}{蓄積|ちくせき}: capital accumulation
- {蓄積|ちくせき}された{経験|けいけん}: accumulated experience

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {溜|た}まる: to accumulate, to pile up — more casual, often implies unwanted buildup
- {貯|た}める: to save up — focuses on deliberate saving, especially money
- {積|つ}み{重|かさ}ねる: to pile up — emphasizes the layering process; often used for efforts or experiences
